name: @nickw8/bash-mcp

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List files in a directory. Returns structured entries with name, size, permissions, and modified date — directories end with '/' and links with '@'. Use nameOnly for names alone, recursive for one level of subdirectories, all to include hidden files.

nameOnly.description: Only return names and types (omit size, permissions, modified)

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (text block only, not the returned payload)

tools.name: tree
tools.description: Show directory structure as a compact tree. Returns structured nodes instead of ASCII art. Use dirsOnly for directory-only view, pattern to filter by glob, maxDepth to control depth.

pattern.description: Only show files matching glob pattern

format.description: Text-block format, payload unaffected (default: bare — paths, dirs end with /)

tools.name: du
tools.description: Show disk usage for paths. Returns one { path, sizeBytes } entry per path, largest-first ordering as du emits it. Use maxDepth to control how deep the summary goes.

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (text block only, not the returned payload)

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Find files by name pattern, type, or modification time. Returns structured list of paths. Use names for multiple glob patterns (OR logic), modifiedWithin for recent files (e.g. '7d', '1h').

pattern.description: Alias for name — filename glob pattern (e.g. '*.ts')

names.description: Multiple filename glob patterns (e.g. ['*.ts', '*.py', '*.sh']). Combined with OR logic.

withMetadata.description: Include size (bytes) and mtime (unix timestamp) for each file

tools.name: rg
tools.description: Search file contents with ripgrep. Returns structured matches with file, line number, and matched text. Far more compact than raw rg output. Use glob (string or array, '!' to exclude) to filter files, ignoreCase for case-insensitive search, filesOnly for just filenames, countPerFile for match counts per file, maxPerFile to cap hits per file. For 'collect all X' tasks use only:true to return just the matched substrings (one row per hit) — add replace ($1 capture groups) to extract structured values.

pattern.description: Required. Regex pattern to search for

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: cwd)

glob.description: File glob filter(s); a string or array. Prefix with '!' to exclude (e.g. ['*.ts','!*.test.ts'])

maxResults.description: Max results to return across all files (default 30). When the cap bites, the response reports the true totalMatches so you can decide whether to narrow the pattern or raise the cap

maxPerFile.description: Cap matches per file (rg --max-count), independent of maxResults — keeps one hot file from dominating

only.description: Return only the matched substring(s), not the whole line — one row per match. Best for collecting tokens (versions, names, URLs)

replace.description: Rewrite each match with this template ($1, $2 capture groups) and return the result; implies only-match extraction

context.description: Lines of context around each match

filesOnly.description: Only return filenames, not matched lines

countPerFile.description: Return match counts grouped by file instead of individual matches

maxLineLength.description: Window matched line text to ~this many chars centered on the match, so long/minified lines don't dump in full (0 = unlimited, default 120)

format.description: Text-block format (payload unaffected): grouped (default for matches, file header once then line+text, ripgrep-style), tsv, json, columnar (keys once), bare (no header). filesOnly defaults to bare, countPerFile to tsv.

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (e.g. ['file','line']); text view only

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files matching a glob pattern. Returns a compact list of paths.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Structured git status: branch, staged/unstaged/untracked files. Replaces parsing raw git status output.

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: Structured git log: commit hash, author, date, message. Compact and parseable. Use range for ref comparisons (e.g. 'main..feature'). Use exclude to filter out commits matching a pattern (e.g. 'ci:').

exclude.description: Exclude commits matching this grep pattern (uses --invert-grep)

withFiles.description: Include list of files changed per commit

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns, e.g. ['shortHash','message'] (text block only, not the returned payload)

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Structured git diff: files changed with insertions/deletions counts. Use base+ref for two-ref comparison (e.g. base='main', ref='feature'). Use path to scope to one or more files or directories.

base.description: Base ref for two-ref comparison. When both ref and base are set, runs git diff <base> <ref>

path.description: Limit diff to one or more files or directories (string or array)

tools.name: git_branches
tools.description: List git branches with current branch marker and last commit info.

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (text block only, not the returned payload)

tools.name: repo_health_summary
tools.description: One-call snapshot of a git working tree: branch, ahead/behind vs upstream, staged/unstaged/untracked counts, recent commits, and the uncommitted diffstat.

commits.description: Number of recent commits to include (default 5)

tools.name: git_pr_context
tools.description: Collect the commits and file changes of a branch vs a base ref (for writing a PR description): commit list, changed files with status, and a diffstat over base...head.

tools.name: kube_get
tools.description: Get Kubernetes resources as structured data. Wraps kubectl get -o json and returns a compact summary by default. Use the jq param to extract specific fields from the raw JSON (e.g. '.spec.template.spec.containers[].env') instead of the summary.

resource.description: Required. Resource type (e.g. pods, deployments, services, nodes)

jq.description: jq filter applied to raw kubectl JSON. Skips the default summary and returns the jq result instead. Example: '.spec.template.spec.containers[].env'

includeLabels.description: Include each resource's labels (default false — labels are verbose and mostly hashes; use selector to filter or jq to read specific ones)

format.description: Text-block format for the item list, payload unaffected (default: tsv)

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns, e.g. ['name','status','restarts'] (text view only)

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: kube_logs
tools.description: Get pod logs. Returns structured log lines with timestamps when available. Use grep to filter lines by regex pattern (e.g. 'ERROR|WARN') instead of piping through shell commands.

grep.description: Regex pattern to filter log lines (e.g. 'ERROR|WARN', 'timeout'). Only matching lines are returned.

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: kube_contexts
tools.description: List available kubectl contexts with current context marked.

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (text block only, not the returned payload)

tools.name: kube_diagnose_pod
tools.description: Diagnose why a pod is unhealthy in one call. Returns status, likely causes, suggested next commands, and evidence (CrashLoopBackOff/ImagePullBackOff/OOMKilled/Unschedulable/restarts).

tools.name: kube_pod_failure_summary
tools.description: List unhealthy pods in a namespace with their failure reason and evidence — one call instead of get + describe per pod.

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: kube_deployment_status
tools.description: Report a deployment's rollout health (ready/desired replicas, conditions) as a structured diagnosis.

tools.name: kube_events_summary
tools.description: Summarize Warning events in a namespace (grouped by reason, ordered by count) instead of scrolling raw kubectl get events.

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: tf_state_list
tools.description: List resources in Terraform state. Returns the resource addresses plus a byType rollup (type, name, and module are all readable from each address, so they are not repeated per resource).

binary.description: Binary to invoke (terraform or tofu). Defaults to $TF_BINARY, else terraform.

format.description: Text-block format, payload unaffected (default: bare — one address per line)

tools.name: tf_show
tools.description: Show current Terraform state as structured JSON. Returns resource summary with types and attributes.

binary.description: Binary to invoke (terraform or tofu). Defaults to $TF_BINARY, else terraform.

tools.name: tf_plan_summary
tools.description: Run terraform plan and return a structured summary of changes (add/change/destroy counts and affected resources).

planFile.description: Path to a saved plan file (from `terraform plan -out`); summarized via `show -json` instead of re-running plan.

binary.description: Binary to invoke (terraform or tofu). Defaults to $TF_BINARY, else terraform.

tools.name: tf_workspaces
tools.description: List Terraform workspaces with current workspace marked.

binary.description: Binary to invoke (terraform or tofu). Defaults to $TF_BINARY, else terraform.

tools.name: tf_outputs
tools.description: List Terraform/OpenTofu outputs (name, value) with sensitive values redacted — a redacted output carries sensitive:true and no value.

binary.description: Binary to invoke (terraform or tofu). Defaults to $TF_BINARY, else terraform.

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (text block only, not the returned payload)

tools.name: tf_providers
tools.description: List the Terraform/OpenTofu version and selected provider versions for the project.

binary.description: Binary to invoke (terraform or tofu). Defaults to $TF_BINARY, else terraform.

tools.name: tf_validate_summary
tools.description: Validate the Terraform/OpenTofu config and return a compact pass/fail summary with diagnostics.

binary.description: Binary to invoke (terraform or tofu). Defaults to $TF_BINARY, else terraform.

tools.name: tf_modules_summary
tools.description: List the modules used by an initialized Terraform/OpenTofu project (key, source, version). Reads .terraform/modules/modules.json — run init first.

tools.name: tf_backend_info
tools.description: Report the configured backend type and config for an initialized project. Reads .terraform/terraform.tfstate — run init first.

tools.name: argo_apps
tools.description: List ArgoCD applications with sync/health status. Structured summary instead of table output.

tools.name: argo_app_detail
tools.description: Get detailed status for a single ArgoCD application including resource health.

tools.name: argo_app_diff
tools.description: Show what's out of sync for an ArgoCD application.

tools.name: argo_app_health_summary
tools.description: Diagnose an ArgoCD application's health in one call: overall sync/health, likely causes, suggested next commands, and the unhealthy resources/conditions as evidence.

tools.name: helm_list
tools.description: List Helm releases with status, chart, and app version. Structured output.

tools.name: helm_status
tools.description: Get detailed status of a Helm release.

tools.name: helm_values
tools.description: Get the computed values for a Helm release as structured data.

tools.name: helm_release_triage
tools.description: Diagnose a Helm release's health in one call: combines helm status + helm history into current status, likely causes, suggested next commands, and recent-revision evidence.

tools.name: jq
tools.description: Query and transform JSON using jq expressions. Accepts a file path or raw JSON string. Returns parsed, structured output — far more compact than reading a full JSON file. The filter is passed directly to jq (no shell), so shell-style escaping such as backslash-escaped quotes is neither needed nor supported — write the filter exactly as jq expects it.

input.description: Raw JSON string to process (alternative to file)

rawOutput.description: Output raw strings without JSON encoding (-r)

tools.name: yq
tools.description: Query and transform YAML files using yq expressions (mikefarah/yq). Outputs as JSON for structured consumption. Far more compact than reading a full YAML file.

input.description: Raw YAML string to process (alternative to file)

tools.name: cat
tools.description: Read one or more files with line numbers and smart truncation. Returns structured output with metadata. Pass `path` for a single file, or `paths` to read several in one call (returns { files, count }) — collapsing what would otherwise be multiple round-trips. For large files, use startLine/endLine or maxLines to limit output. Use ref to read from a git branch/commit instead of disk (e.g. ref='main'). NOTE: reading with cat does NOT satisfy the built-in Edit/Write "must read first" guard (it tracks only the built-in Read tool) — run the built-in Read on a file immediately before editing it.

paths.description: Read multiple files in one call; a string or array. Returns { files, count }; a per-file failure is reported in that file's `error` and does not abort the others.

ref.description: Git ref to read from (e.g. 'main', 'HEAD~1', a commit hash). When set, reads file content from git (git show ref:path) instead of disk.

maxLines.description: Max lines to return per file (default 200, use 0 for unlimited)

lineNumbers.description: Prepend line numbers to each line (useful when locating a line). Does not register the file as read for the built-in Edit — use the built-in Read right before editing.

tools.name: outline
tools.description: Show the structural outline of a file — function/class names, top-level comments, imports. Returns a compact view without implementation bodies. Includes git metadata (branch, commit) when the file is in a git repo. Use instead of cat when reviewing file structure or auditing many files at once.

ref.description: Git ref to outline (e.g. 'main', 'HEAD~1', a commit hash). When set, reads file content from git (git show ref:path) instead of disk.

tools.name: run
tools.description: Run a single command — a binary plus an args array, executed directly without a shell (so no pipes, redirects, or ';'/'&&' in the string) — and return structured output with smart truncation. Pass the binary as `command` and its arguments as `args` (e.g. command='npm', args=['test']); for a real shell pipeline run the shell yourself: command='sh', args=['-c', 'a | b > c']. Keeps the last N lines of output by default (where errors typically appear), or the first N with mode='head'. Use for build, test, and lint commands where you need exit code and error details, not full verbose output.

command.description: The binary to execute — NOT a shell string (e.g. 'npm', 'git', 'sh'). For pipes/redirects, use command='sh' and put the script in args.

args.description: Arguments passed directly to the binary (e.g. ['test']). With command='sh', use ['-c', '<shell script>'].

maxLines.description: Max stdout/stderr lines to keep. 0 = unlimited.

mode.description: Keep the last N lines (tail, default) or the first N (head).

maxBytes.description: Optional cap on stdout/stderr byte length (UTF-8).

tools.name: run_seq
tools.description: Run an ordered list of labeled commands one after another, stopping at the first failure by default. Use for dependent steps (e.g. build then test then package) where order matters and a later step is pointless if an earlier one fails. Unlike batch (parallel), run_seq is sequential and short-circuits; set stopOnError=false to run every step regardless.

command.description: The binary to execute — NOT a shell string (e.g. 'npm', 'sh'). For pipes/redirects in a step, use command='sh' with args=['-c', '<script>'].

args.description: Arguments passed directly to the binary (e.g. ['test']). With command='sh', use ['-c', '<shell script>'].

label.description: Label for this step in the results (defaults to the command name)

steps.description: Required. Ordered steps to run sequentially

stopOnError.description: Stop at the first step with a non-zero exit code (default true).

maxLines.description: Max stdout/stderr lines to keep per step. 0 = unlimited.

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Run multiple commands in parallel and return all results. Each command is a binary plus an args array, executed without a shell (for a pipeline use command='sh', args=['-c', '...']). Use when you need to gather independent pieces of information in a single tool call instead of multiple sequential calls.

command.description: The binary to execute — NOT a shell string (e.g. 'git', 'sh'). For pipes/redirects, use command='sh' with args=['-c', '<script>'].

label.description: Label for this command in the results (defaults to the command name)

tools.name: git_diff_content
tools.description: Show git diff with structured patch content. Returns parsed hunks per file instead of raw unified diff text. Use this when you need to see actual code changes, not just file-level stats. Use base+ref for two-ref comparison (e.g. base='main', ref='feature'). Use path to scope to one or more files or directories.

ref.description: Diff against this ref (e.g. 'HEAD~1', 'main', a commit hash)

base.description: Base ref for two-ref comparison. When both ref and base are set, runs git diff <base> <ref>

path.description: Limit diff to one or more files or directories (string or array)

context.description: Number of context lines around changes (passed as -U<n>)

tools.name: npm_lint
tools.description: Run biome check and return structured diagnostics with file, line, column, message, and rule. Far more compact and parseable than raw lint output. Use minSeverity to filter by severity level.

paths.description: Specific path(s) to lint; a string or array (default: '.')

minSeverity.description: Minimum severity to include (e.g. 'error' drops warnings and info)

format.description: Text-block format (payload unaffected): grouped (default, file header once then line:col rule message), tsv, or json

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (e.g. ['file','loc','message']) — affects the text block only, not the returned payload

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: npm_test
tools.description: Run vitest or jest (picked from package.json) and return structured test results: suites, pass/fail counts, failure messages. Much more compact than raw test output. Only failures are listed by default; use verbose=true for all tests.

verbose.description: Include all tests in output (default: only failures)

tools.name: npm_typecheck
tools.description: Run tsc/tsgo --noEmit and return structured type errors with file, line, column, message, and TS error code. Much more compact than raw tsc output. Auto-detects tsgo for faster checking. Use project to specify a tsconfig.

project.description: Path to tsconfig.json (default: auto-detected by tsc)

format.description: Text-block format (payload unaffected): grouped (default, file header once then line:col rule message), tsv, or json

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (e.g. ['file','loc','message']) — affects the text block only, not the returned payload

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: dotnet_build
tools.description: Run dotnet build and return structured diagnostics with file, line, column, message, and error code. Much more compact than raw MSBuild output. Warnings are omitted by default; pass includeWarnings:true (or detailLevel:'full') to include them.

project.description: Path to .csproj or .sln file (default: auto-detected in cwd)

includeWarnings.description: Include warnings in the response (default: errors only, even on a successful build)

format.description: Text-block format (payload unaffected): grouped (default, file header once then line:col rule message), tsv, or json

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (e.g. ['file','loc','message']) — affects the text block only, not the returned payload

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: dotnet_test
tools.description: Run dotnet test and return structured results: pass/fail/skip counts, failure messages. Much more compact than raw test output. Only failures are listed.

project.description: Path to .csproj or .sln file (default: auto-detected in cwd)

tools.name: liquibase_validate
tools.description: Validate a Liquibase changelog and return a structured pass/fail result with per-changeset errors (duplicate ids, checksum drift). Much more compact than raw output. liquibase is on PATH — no mise/wrapper needed.

cwd.description: Directory to run liquibase in (where the defaults file / changelog live).

defaultsFile.description: Path to the Liquibase defaults file (--defaults-file), e.g. db-dev.properties. Usually carries the JDBC URL, credentials, and changelog path.

changelogFile.description: Changelog path (--changelog-file); usually set in the defaults file instead.

extraArgs.description: Additional raw arguments appended to the liquibase invocation.

tools.name: liquibase_update_sql
tools.description: Render the SQL Liquibase would run for pending changesets (updateSQL) as structured per-changeset summaries with a SQL-Server batch lint. Does NOT apply changes. SQL bodies are omitted unless includeRaw or changesetId is set. liquibase is on PATH — no mise/wrapper needed.

cwd.description: Directory to run liquibase in (where the defaults file / changelog live).

defaultsFile.description: Path to the Liquibase defaults file (--defaults-file), e.g. db-dev.properties. Usually carries the JDBC URL, credentials, and changelog path.

changelogFile.description: Changelog path (--changelog-file); usually set in the defaults file instead.

extraArgs.description: Additional raw arguments appended to the liquibase invocation.

changesetId.description: Return only this changeset's full rendered SQL (matches the changeset id).

batchLint.description: Lint each changeset for the SQL-Server 'routine DDL must lead its GO-batch' rule (default true).

detailLevel.description: Output size preset: summary (~20 items), normal (~100), full (uncapped, default).

maxItems.description: Explicit cap on returned items; overrides detailLevel.

tools.name: liquibase_status
tools.description: List Liquibase changesets not yet applied to the target database, as structured JSON. Reports up-to-date vs a pending list. liquibase is on PATH — no mise/wrapper needed.

cwd.description: Directory to run liquibase in (where the defaults file / changelog live).

defaultsFile.description: Path to the Liquibase defaults file (--defaults-file), e.g. db-dev.properties. Usually carries the JDBC URL, credentials, and changelog path.

changelogFile.description: Changelog path (--changelog-file); usually set in the defaults file instead.

extraArgs.description: Additional raw arguments appended to the liquibase invocation.

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (e.g. ['file','loc','message']) — affects the text block only, not the returned payload

tools.description: Run shellcheck and return structured diagnostics with file, line, column, message, and SC rule code. Much more compact than raw shellcheck output. Use minSeverity to filter by severity level.

files.description: Required. Shell script path(s) to lint; a string or array

minSeverity.description: Minimum severity to include (e.g. 'error' drops warnings and info)

format.description: Text-block format (payload unaffected): grouped (default, file header once then line:col rule message), tsv, or json

fields.description: Limit the text view to these columns (e.g. ['file','loc','message']) — affects the text block only, not the returned payload

tools.description: Run a shell test script — bats `.bats` files via `--tap`, or a plain `.sh` harness — and return structured results: per-case pass/fail plus a summary parsed from TAP or `N tests, M failures` output, falling back to exit-code-only when the format is unrecognized. Executes the script, so it is gated by BASH_MCP_MODE.

tools.name: check_environment
tools.description: Report which CLIs are installed (and their versions) so you can pick the right tool before calling it. Probes are client-only and non-blocking — no server/auth calls. Includes kubectl's current context when available.

tools.name: list_guidance
tools.description: Return an intent → preferred-tool index so you can pick the right bash-mcp tool for a goal. Each entry names the tool to prefer, raw-command anti-patterns to avoid, and why. Filter with `intent` (substring) or `category` to narrow the list.

intent.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the intent text.

tools.name: gh_pr_checks
tools.description: Report a pull request's CI checks as counts per state plus the failing and pending checks. Defaults to the current branch's PR; passing checks are counted, not listed, unless all=true.

pr.description: PR number, URL or branch (default: the current branch's PR)

all.description: List passing and skipped checks too (default: only the rest)

cwd.description: Repository path (default: the server's working directory)

tools.name: gh_run_failure_summary
tools.description: Diagnose a GitHub Actions run in one call: status, the failed jobs and steps, and the ##[error] lines from the failed log as evidence. Defaults to the latest run on the current branch.

run.description: Run ID (default: the latest run on `branch`)

branch.description: Branch whose latest run to read (default: the current branch)

cwd.description: Repository path (default: the server's working directory)

tools.name: glab_ci_status
tools.description: Report a GitLab pipeline's jobs as counts per status plus the failed, running and pending jobs. Defaults to the current branch's latest pipeline; pass mr for a merge request's head pipeline. Passing, skipped and manual jobs are counted, not listed, unless all=true.

pipeline.description: Pipeline ID (default: the latest pipeline on `branch`)

mr.description: Merge request IID: read its head pipeline instead

branch.description: Branch whose latest pipeline to read (default: current branch)

repo.description: GROUP/REPO or URL (default: the repo at `cwd`)

cwd.description: Repository path (default: the server's working directory)

all.description: List passing, skipped and manual jobs too

tools.name: glab_pipeline_failure_summary
tools.description: Diagnose a GitLab pipeline in one call: status, the failed jobs and why GitLab says they failed, and the last script lines of each failed job's trace as evidence. Allowed-to-fail jobs are noted, not counted as the failure. Defaults to the current branch's latest pipeline.

pipeline.description: Pipeline ID (default: the latest pipeline on `branch`)

mr.description: Merge request IID: read its head pipeline instead

branch.description: Branch whose latest pipeline to read (default: current branch)

repo.description: GROUP/REPO or URL (default: the repo at `cwd`)

cwd.description: Repository path (default: the server's working directory)

instructions: Structured CLI wrappers that return JSON instead of raw text. Philosophy: reach for a structured tool first; `run`/`batch` are the escape hatch for commands without a dedicated wrapper. Prefer a diagnostic tool (one call that returns status + likely causes + suggested next commands + evidence) over chaining raw commands and reasoning across their output yourself. Prefer these over raw Bash for structured output and lower token usage; call check_environment for which CLIs are installed, and list_guidance for the intent→preferred-tool index. Caveat: reading a file with cat does NOT satisfy the built-in Edit/Write "must read first" guard (it tracks only the built-in Read tool) — use the built-in Read on a file immediately before editing it. Config: BASH_MCP_LOG (error|info|off) controls wide-event logging to stderr; BASH_MCP_MODE (readOnly|confirmWrites|off, default readOnly) gates run/batch.
